Let me solve the problem first. John sublets to 3 people at $400/month each = $1200/month income. He pays $900/month rent. Monthly profit = $1200 - $900 = $300. Yearly profit = $300 × 12 = $3,600.

The student's incorrect solution: computes $1200/month from subletting, then adds the $900 rent he pays as if it were part of his earnings: $1200 + $900 = $2100. Then $2100 × 12 = $25,200. Then subtracts rent paid $900 × 12 = $10,800, getting $14,400. Note: $14,400 is actually 1200 × 12 — the income, not the profit. The error is including the $900 rent in his earnings (adding it), which double-counts it: he adds it then subtracts it, canceling out, so the "profit" ends up being gross income.

What's the belief? The student treats the $900 rent as part of John's earnings ("His total monthly earnings from the apartment is $1200 + $900 = $2100"). This is a comprehension error about what the $900 represents — rent he pays is a cost, money going out, not earnings. The arithmetic is internally coherent given the wrong belief (he adds 900 then later subtracts the same 900, so it cancels; the mistake is the model of earnings).

Routing: comprehension vs wrong operation — is the working wrong given what he believes? He believes the $900 is part of total earnings. Given that belief, his arithmetic $1200 + $900 = $2100, ×12, then subtract rent = $14,400 is correct on his belief. So comprehension. Actually, wait — could it be argued that the belief is "profit = income - expenses" and he knows rent is an expense? He explicitly says "But he also pays rent" and subtracts it. Yet he adds it to earnings too. Under his own chain, adding the rent to earnings then subtracting it is inconsistent with his own stated understanding that rent is paid by John. Hmm. But the demonstrable enactment is that he treats the $900 as a component of "total monthly earnings from the apartment" — he labels the $2100 as earnings. The tutor repeatedly points out "you included the $900 John pays in rent each month as a profit." The student persists for many turns, reasserting $14,400 even while saying he understands, and finally at turn 4 produces the correct chain with "His total monthly earnings from the apartment is $1200, not $2100... profit is $14,400 - $10,800 = $3,600."
